evaluations.reason: Destruction will come upon people suddenly: an outward event arriving; no inner-being operation is named or qualified by 'come upon'.
Labor pains come upon a woman: a bodily event arriving; no inner-being operation is named or qualified.
Jeroboam sends an ambush to come upon Judah from behind: an outward attack carried out, enacting a hostile purpose of another party.

The wrath of the Lord did not come upon them after Hezekiah humbled himself: the coming of an inner state of the other (wrath), negated, is the matter; the humbling is told by other words of the verse.
Evil that has come upon David from his youth: calamity befalling; no inner-being operation is named or qualified by 'come upon'.
Tribulation and these things come upon the people in the latter days: events arriving; the returning and obeying are other words of the verse.
The locusts come upon the land of Egypt: an outward plague arriving; no inner-being operation.
'Why have these things come upon me?': the calamity that arrived is the content of the question; 'come upon' names the event, not the saying in the heart.
The Lord brought disaster upon them: the consequence arriving; the disobedience is told by other words.
No razor shall come upon the head of the Nazirite: an outward matter of a vow; no inner-being operation.
No razor shall come upon the head of the Nazirite: an outward matter of a vow; no inner-being operation (the unit is shared with another code).
My spirit within me earnestly seeks you: the spirit's earnest seeking of God, the seeking is itself the inner operation.
Your brothers will find compassion with their captors: what is found is an inner state of the other (compassion); it bears on the inner being without being the operation.
Love does not insist on its own way: the will's demand for its own way, negated; the absence of insisting is what the verse states.
Barnabas goes to Tarsus to look for Saul: an outward search for a person, with the person as the end of the search (relational target).
Look for a man of Tarsus named Saul: an outward search for a person named; the person is the relational target.
Shall we look for another?: the expecting of the one who is to come, asked by John's disciples; the expectation is itself the inner operation.
Shall we look for another?: the expecting of the one who is to come; the expectation is itself the inner operation.
Shall we look for another?: John asks whether to go on expecting the one who is to come; the expectation is itself the inner operation.
Three men are looking for you: an outward search for a person (Peter); the person is the relational target.
I am the one you are looking for: the person sought is the relational target of the men's search.
Joseph was himself looking for the kingdom of God: an expectant waiting directed to the kingdom; the expecting is itself the inner operation.
Saul more handsome than any man: bodily appearance compared; no inner-being operation.
You seek out my iniquity and search for my sin: God's purposed searching for the man's fault, as Job says it; the direction of the searching is the matter.
Herod searched for Peter and did not find him: an outward hunt carried out to seize him, enacting Herod's purpose.
Mary and Joseph returned to Jerusalem searching for the boy: an outward search for a person; the person is the relational target.
The nations of the world seek after these things (food, drink, clothing): a desire and pursuit of the will directed to objects.
Those who seek for glory and honor and immortality by patience in well-doing: a purposed seeking, the direction of the will.
They will seek me diligently but will not find me: the seeking of the Lord, diligent and too late; the seeking is itself the inner operation.
Those who seek me diligently find me: the seeking of wisdom, diligent; the seeking is itself the inner operation.
Observe and seek out all the commandments of the Lord: a purposed seeking, the will turned to the commandments.
Seek out a man who is skillful in playing the lyre: an outward search commissioned for a person; the person is the relational target.
As a shepherd seeks out his flock, so I will seek out my sheep: the Lord's purposed seeking of his scattered people, to rescue them.
To seek shelter in the shadow of Egypt without asking the Lord: a purposed turning to another for protection, the direction of the will.
This generation seeks for a sign: a desire of the will directed to a sign.
An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign: a desire of the will directed to a sign.
No one seeks for God: the absence of seeking is the state named.
As a shepherd seeks out his flock: a purposed seeking with care for the scattered sheep.
He seeks out a skillful craftsman to set up an idol: an outward search for a person; the craftsman is the relational target.
Though you be sought for, you will never be found again: Tyre's end told; no inner-being operation is voiced by 'sought for'.
The Lord has sought out a man after his own heart: the Lord's purposed seeking and choosing of a man; the seeking is the operation.
Let beautiful young virgins be sought out for the king: an outward search commissioned for persons; the persons are the relational target.
You shall be called Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken: a name stating the regard of the Lord toward the city; an inner state of the other, given as a name.
The man who would not make God his refuge sought refuge in his own destruction: a purposed turning of the will for security to the wrong thing.
If he is well disposed toward David: the attitude of favour in Saul's mind toward David; the disposition is the inner state named.
